summary: Unexpected OAuth app scope escalation observed during vendor onboarding flow
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 at ~03:40 UTC automated anomaly detection flagged a surge of admin-scoped API requests originating from a freshly onboarded vendor OAuth app. The app had been granted only 'read:user' and 'email' scopes during onboarding, but tokens observed in logs were accepted for admin-level endpoints.

Impact: Potential lateral privilege escalation allowing the vendor app to call internal admin APIs (user invite, service-token provisioning). Preliminary evidence indicates limited exploratory calls; no confirmed data exfiltration. Affected surface: internal admin API endpoints and service-account provisioning flows in prod-us-east.

Initial detection: SRE alert (anomaly-score > 0.9) for elevated 401->200 pattern on /internal/admin/* endpoints linked to token issuer 'vendor-oauth-app-7b3'.

Why this ticket: Centralize triage, coordinate token revocation, audits, and vendor coordination. Document timeline and remediation steps for potential IR and post-incident review.
timeline:
2026-03-12 03:12 UTC - New OAuth app onboarding completed via self-serve vendor portal.
2026-03-12 03:40 UTC - Anomaly detection flagged unusual admin API success rate.
2026-03-12 03:45 UTC - Support analyst (J. Patel) created temporary block for the app in the proxy layer.
2026-03-12 04:05 UTC - Security Ops began live investigation; initial token revocation started.
2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Additional tokens from same app used in a different IP / ASN pair.
2026-03-14 02:00 UTC - Forensics completed partial scope audit; evidence of scope mismatch between consent record and token introspection results.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate onboarding via vendor portal with scopes 'read:user' and 'email'.
2) Exchange auth code for token via standard flow.
3) Attempt to call /internal/admin/users - expected 403; observed 200 when token is used after service-side proxy handshake.
Note: reproduction requires the exact onboarding flow and proxy headers used in prod; do not run in staging without coordination.
logs:
Auth server introspection (2026-03-12T03:37:12Z): token_id=tok_7b3_abcd, client_id=vendor-oauth-app-7b3, scopes=read:user email, issued_at=2026-03-12T03:12:44Z
Proxy access log (2026-03-12T03:39:18Z): src_ip=18.205.2.9, x-auth-client=vendor-oauth-app-7b3, request=/internal/admin/invite, status=200, backend_user=service-proxy
IAM audit (2026-03-13T09:07:01Z): service_account_created by token=tok_7b3_abcd, target=svc-analytics-temp, role=admin.write
Token introspection mismatch (2026-03-14T01:56:12Z): introspected_scopes=read:user email offline_access admin.write (introspection returned extra scope 'admin.write' that was not present in consent record).
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Proxy header elevation bug - the proxy maps vendor client to an internal service identity when a specific header handshake occurs during onboarding, inadvertently granting broader permissions.
Hypothesis 2: Consent-chaining vulnerability - incremental consent or a refresh exchange produced a token with aggregated scopes.
Evidence so far: token introspection shows 'admin.write' present despite consent record; proxy logs contain a previously undocumented header 'x-internal-bridge: onboarding-step' correlated with successful admin calls.
Next steps: replicate minimal repro in isolated env, capture full token exchange traces, review proxy header handling code path, patch to drop internal-bridge header for third-party clients.
comments: 2026-03-12 04:20 - J. Patel (Support): Temporarily blocked client_id vendor-oauth-app-7b3 at API gateway. Customers using similar onboarding flow notified via #support-private.
2026-03-12 05:10 - A. Singh (SRE): Collected gzip logs and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-sec/forensics/INT-915234/production-logs-20260312.tar.gz

2026-03-13 10:00 - L. Morales (Security Ops): Confirmed creation of a service_account with admin role using token tok_7b3_abcd. We rotated affected service tokens and disabled the vendor app in identity provider.
Action: require vendor to re-auth and sign new consent after fix.

2026-03-14 01:30 - R. Ortega (Assignee): Replication plan in place; spinning up isolated cluster to exercise onboarding handshake. Patch candidate to strip 'x-internal-bridge' header in proxy-next branch (PR forthcoming).
2026-03-14 09:00 - M. Chen (Reporter): Notifying Legal and Compliance as per incident classification; preserving chain-of-custody for logs.
resolution: Mitigations in progress: vendor app disabled in IDP, revoked active tokens tied to client_id vendor-oauth-app-7b3, rotated implicated service account credentials, applied temporary rule to drop 'x-internal-bridge' header at API gateway. Full code patch submitted to proxy-next to permanently enforce header stripping for third-party clients.
resolution_notes: Immediate: tokens revoked and app disabled (2026-03-12). Medium: proxy rule applied to drop internal-bridge header (2026-03-13). Long-term: code change (PR #4821) to enforce header hygiene + unit tests and a mandatory onboarding validation checklist for vendor apps. Post-incident: schedule blameless postmortem and vendor re-onboarding process updates. No confirmed data exfiltration observed; investigation continuing for scope of created service account actions.
follow_up_actions:
1) Deploy proxy-next patch to prod and monitor for similar anomalies for 72h.
2) Update vendor onboarding runbook to require ephemeral onboarding tokens and deny persistence of offline_access by default.
3) Add automated drift check comparing consent records to token introspection once per minute for new clients.
4) Postmortem and update confluence page with timeline and remediation steps.
metrics_observed:
Spike in admin endpoint success rate from new client: baseline 0.01 req/min -> 2.4 req/min during window.
Number of tokens revoked: 4.
Service accounts created: 1 (svc-analytics-temp).
notes_for_audit: All relevant logs archived in s3://redwood-sec/forensics/INT-915234. Access to archive restricted to Security Ops and SRE. Evidence checklist attached in confluence page. Legal advised to hold vendor contract communications until investigation completes.
